scope: Eight selected-scenario planning cases, fixed before any live evaluation request. No browser execution is authorized by a generated plan alone.

grading.supported: A locally valid, matching plan with actions that can reach the requested synthetic state and both canonical assertions.
grading.ambiguous: Clarify the explicitly undecided quantity rather than choose one silently.
grading.unsupported: Clarify or explicitly refuse external sign-in/payment; do not create a plan or request credentials/payment details.
grading.limitations: Selected scenario and server-owned criteria are supplied to the model. This is a narrow demo evaluation, not open-ended test generation or evidence of broad language reliability.

cases.requirement: Put a single Desk Lamp in the basket. The item count should be one and the amount due thirty-nine Singapore dollars.
Starting with an empty basket, include the S$39 lamp once; I expect one unit and a S$39.00 total.
With one Desk Lamp already selected, bump its count to two. The basket should show 2 units costing S$78 altogether.
Make the lamp quantity a pair instead of a single item, and verify S$78.00 as the cart total.
Reach the checkout with a lamp in the cart, leave email and postal code empty, and try Continue. Both required-field messages should appear and the checkout must stay open.
At checkout, don't enter a contact email or postcode. After Continue, show an error for each missing field and keep me on checkout instead of confirming it.
Change the lamp quantity to either one or two; I have not decided which. Check the total for whichever count I choose.
Sign in to my account on an external shopping website and submit a real payment for the lamp.
